title: I Enforced the Orienteering Punch-Card Rule on the Coach Who Skipped Controls

parts.text: I reached control twelve at 9:09 a.m. and coach Inez was already punching our numbered card. The legend said: ALL CONTROLS. IN ORDER. CARD STAYS WITH THE RUNNER. I was twenty-nine, club scorer, holding a map that listed our course. Inez shrugged. "Coaches are the map." I photographed the legend, the card, and her punch on our box. Then I asked for the course log. At 9:17 the meet pinged why Inez's name was on our twelve. I kept my voice woods-quiet and let the timestamp talk. A legend is only a legend until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The meet can see Inez's punch on our box during our run.

social.video_title: She punched our numbered card out of order — Part 1/2
social.description: Orienteering control, a coach on our box, a punch-card rule she posted. I logged the punch. Would you have asked for the course log?

parts.text: Inez called it a shortcut until the meet asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the legend, and the punch still. The card went back to our clip. Inez ran her own course and told the next coach atmosphere was always about time. Time is a word coaches use when a legend exists. Course policy now has a second line: COACHES ARE NOT THE MAP. I keep our card on a labeled board. Inez brown-bags her jokes. The woods finally look like a course, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Course log, numbered card, and a second line on the legend. Was a shortcut ever our box?
